summary: Charlottetown's east side is institutional and industrial along the Hillsborough River: the QEH (white metal 1980s blocks, red EMERGENCY/URGENCE canopy), the district heating plant with its stacks and rusty blue-domed silo (a $180M replacement going up beside it for 2028), Access PEI and the Liquor Commission off Riverside Drive, and the arena/racetrack/event grounds on Kensington Road (navy metal over brick; Red Shores in white and red with a red canopy). Behind it are 1970s-90s suburbs (Hillsborough Park, East Royalty) with new four-storey apartments and townhouses, and across the bridge the western edge of Stratford: Southport's highway strip and Bunbury Mall; the Stratford Town Centre and Kinlock Plaza lie past the map's east edge.

buildings.name: Queen Elizabeth Hospital, 60 Riverside Drive
buildings.facts: Opened April 1982, replacing the old Charlottetown and PEI hospitals; 243-245 acute beds. Main entrance off Riverside Drive upgraded and ER expanded around 2006. Mental Health and Addictions ER opened Feb 2024 inside the same building as the ER (separate space). $1.1M OR/air renovation and >$2M partial roof replacement announced Jan 2021. Declared over capacity repeatedly (Nov 2023, June 2023: all 245 beds full, 15 admitted patients stuck in ER). AI weapons scanner made permanent at the ER doors April 2026 after a 2-week pilot found 30+ weapons. Oct 2026: imaging patients must now register at central admitting by the main entrance first, 30 minutes early. Dec 2025: $1M donation for cafeteria, a 'music corner' and a staff outdoor terrace. Heated by the district heating plant on Riverside Drive. 2026-27 capital budget: $43.2M to upgrade the QEH's building operations.
buildings.look: A big sprawl of 1980s blocks, mostly 3-5 storeys, clad in white and very light grey metal panels with ribbed metal bands, flat roofs with mechanical penthouses and vents. Main entrance (photo, 2026): a tall glass atrium of 4 storeys framed in white, with a long low white space-frame glass canopy over the drop-off, flagpoles (Canada, PEI) in front, and orange-yellow accent panels on the block corners either side. Emergency entrance (photos 2021, 2023, 2024): a flat white canopy on square white posts across the front of a one-storey grey-metal-panel wing, 'EMERGENCY / URGENCE' in big red capitals on the canopy's white fascia (wrapping onto its side too), a glass vestibule with sliding doors under it, concrete jersey barriers and an ambulance bay beside.

buildings.name: Eastlink Centre (the arena) and Red Shores casino/grandstand, Kensington Road
buildings.facts: Opened as the main venue of the 1991 Canada Winter Games; home of the QMJHL Charlottetown Islanders; ~4,000 seats. City owns the rink, province the trade centre half. 2019 city voted to dissolve its board; 2020 Atlantic Lottery looked at buying the trade-centre portion. $54.9M modernization: Ottawa said July 2026 it's ready to fund its share; Nov 25 2026 city agreed to cover interest on an ~$18M loan; construction to start April 2027: more than 5,000 seats, new lobby, reworked front entrance, walking track, new HVAC/ice plant, emergency shelter for 1,000+. Hub of Old Home Week (August) with the fair on Red Shores/Eastlink property. Red Shores Racetrack and Casino (58 Kensington Road, Charlottetown Driving Park, owned by Atlantic Lottery since 2005) is next door; whether OSM's 13,080 m2 footprint includes the casino/grandstand is unclear: no separate casino footprint is in the list.
buildings.look: Arena: lower walls red-brown brick (split-face block look) with two pale tan bands, upper walls and the big box of the bowl in navy-blue ribbed metal siding (dark green-grey in older photos). White lowercase 'eastlink centre' with 'Charlottetown' below on the navy metal over a loading dock (photo 2026); a red-painted steel portal frame (two red columns, beams sloping up to the wall) over the glass doors of a main entrance, 'WELCOME' banner. Flat/very low roof. Red Shores (photo 2020): a front with a red standing-seam curved canopy on red brick-and-stone piers over the doors, walls of white/light grey panels with big dark-red panels and a gold-red swoosh, 'RED SHORES Racetrack & Casino' sign in red on white over the canopy, ribbon windows, beige ledgestone base; 'TRACKSIDE patio' sign at left. Judges' stand at the track (photo): two-storey white tower with green trim bands and a dark green pyramid roof with a weathervane, bunting on its balcony. Casino had an 8,000 sq ft expansion (new dining/entertainment) from 2025, due early 2026.

buildings.name: PEI Brewing Company, 96 Kensington Road at Garfield Street
buildings.facts: Island's oldest craft brewery (offshoot of downtown's Gahan House), moved to Kensington Road ~2012-13 (first cans 2013); expanded with government loans 2013 ($2M) and 2019 ($746k). Taproom with cold beer store, growlers, pizza oven, event space. A big window at the front shows the brewhouse to Kensington Road. Hell Street beer named for Dorchester Street.
buildings.look: Guess: a converted one/two-storey industrial building, light grey or charcoal metal siding with a wood-clad or dark taproom front, a big glass window onto the shiny steel tanks facing Kensington Road, the brewery's name in big letters over it; loading docks and a tank farm at the back.

buildings.name: District heating plant (PEI Energy Systems, run by Enwave), Riverside Drive
buildings.facts: Burns garbage and wood chips since 1983 to heat ~145 buildings downtown incl. the QEH and City Hall. A $180M replacement waste-to-energy plant (Enwave, Canada Infrastructure Bank loan, province and city) is to be built on the same Riverside Drive site, on the shore point across the yard from the old plant; announced Sept 2025, construction from late 2025/early 2026, working 2028, double the capacity, take 90% of the Island's burnable waste. The old plant (42 years old) stays, decommissioned. The project had been 'three years behind schedule and millions over budget' already in 2022. May 2026: Island Waste says the landfill could last 22 more years with it.
buildings.look: Old plant (photos): a cluster of flat-roofed blocks in white and cream-painted concrete and pale metal, one taller (3-4 storey equivalent) boiler block, several thin dark steel stacks (5 or 6, one tall), sloped-roof tipping bays with big dark openings for the garbage trucks on the street side, a beige metal-clad shed with overhead doors at the water end, a big insulated silver duct elbow by the lot. Beside it, a round wood-chip silo ~15 m high, white/grey steel badly rust-streaked, with a blue domed top. Chain-link fence, flat gravel and asphalt yard by the river shore (red sandstone riprap). A sign on the fence: 'Powering Possibility / Future Home of PEI's New Waste-to-Energy Facility' with the blue 'enwave' wordmark.

buildings.name: Hillsborough Park Community Centre
buildings.facts: City-owned hall: public meetings (the 2023 Hillsborough Park housing consultation), fitness classes, Vaisakhi celebrations; got a gender-neutral washroom. Interior photo 2023: a gym-like hall with green-cushioned chairs, white block walls, artwork. Pickleball courts beside it opened Aug 8 2024; a fenced off-leash dog park off Acadian Drive since 2017.

buildings.facts: Moved into the former PEILCC liquor store in Bunbury Mall; earlier (2008) in a building the mayor said 'was a garden shed at some point'. Has a remote panic button (2026). buildings.look: Three or four storeys, vinyl siding: brown/taupe on the older ones (Elena Court was brown siding with white trim), white with a black top floor on the newer ones; balconies, flat or low hipped roofs.

suggested._note: older ones: colour #8b7a68, trim white, roof hipped, roof_colour #4a4a4a

buildings.name: New townhouse row, north-east East Royalty / Hillsborough Park edge
buildings.facts: OSM ids from 2024: built after the 2020 lidar, so no measured height. Possibly an early piece of the province's Hillsborough Park development (1,100-1,476 units planned in phases on 34 ha, Fathom Studio master plan, 2023-), or a private subdivision.
buildings.look: Two-storey townhouse rows, each unit with its own front door and small porch; vinyl siding alternating in greys, blue-grey and white, some board-and-batten, gabled asphalt roofs in charcoal.

neighbourhoods.name: Hillsborough Park
neighbourhoods.where: north-east Charlottetown along the river: Acadian Drive, Westcomb Crescent, Northridge Parkway, Hunter Lane, Longboat Drive
neighbourhoods.look: 1970s-80s suburb: one-storey bungalows and split-levels, some 1.5-storey Cape Cods, vinyl siding in white, beige, pale blue and grey with dark shutters, charcoal or brown asphalt roofs, driveways, lawns, a few big maples; a couple of three-storey 1980s walk-up apartment blocks. Province-owned 34 ha between it and Wright's Creek is planned for 1,100-1,476 units (single homes, townhouses, apartments, village square, 100 m creek buffer); for now mostly field and woods.

neighbourhoods.name: East Royalty
neighbourhoods.where: both sides of St Peters Road north of the bypass, out to the edge of the map
neighbourhoods.look: 1990s-2010s subdivisions: two-storey and split-entry houses in vinyl siding (greys, taupe, sage, white), attached garages, darker roofs; three/four-storey apartment blocks near St Peters Road and the bypass (brown or white siding, some with black top floors), a small commercial strip (KFC, pharmacy) at St Peters Road.

neighbourhoods.name: Riverside Drive / Kensington Road industrial
neighbourhoods.where: between the Hillsborough Bridge approach, Riverside Drive, Kensington Road, Garfield Street and Walker Drive
neighbourhoods.look: Flat steel warehouses and shops in beige, white and grey, the brewery, government offices (Access PEI), the heating plant and oil tanks by the water, car dealers along Riverside Drive; chain-link fences, gravel yards, truck trailers.

neighbourhoods.name: Southport (Stratford)
neighbourhoods.where: the Stratford end of the Hillsborough Bridge: Stratford Road, Hopeton Road, Michael Thomas Way, the waterfront
neighbourhoods.look: Old cottage area turned highway commercial: gas bars, fast food, a motel and plazas on Stratford Road, 1950s-70s bungalows and storey-and-a-half houses behind (white or pastel siding), new 4-5 storey apartments on the waterfront and off Stratford Road.

neighbourhoods.name: Stratford west (Bunbury, Glen Stewart)
neighbourhoods.where: Hopeton Road, Glen Stewart Drive, Bunbury Road to the map's east edge
neighbourhoods.look: 1980s-2010s subdivisions: two-storey houses and bungalows in vinyl siding (greys, whites, blues), attached garages, black or brown roofs; the town's newer houses are bigger and greyer.

current_events.what: Eastlink Centre $54.9M modernization: city agreed Nov 25 2026 to cover interest on an ~$18M loan; Ottawa 'ready to help' (July 2026: 'we're not looking for a grant, we're looking for an investment'); construction from April 2027. Built 1991; the local MP: 'this is a 1991 building in 2026'.

Red Shores casino profit fell ~35% to $2.5M in 2024-25; Atlantic Lottery blamed the cost of living ('visits consistent... amount spent at each visit is down') and its own 8,000 sq ft renovation (no new slot machines; new dining), due early 2026. The province says the renovation 'will create a healthier play space'.
Hillsborough Hospital replacement: promised 'immediately' in 2019, cost from $100M to $200M to over $271M, scaled back (cheaper interior materials), opening late 2027/2028.
current_events.where: mental health campus beside the QEH

current_events.what: QEH: over capacity repeatedly; waits of 15-22 hours; AI weapons scanner at the ER doors (April 2026); imaging patients must now register at central admitting first (Oct 2026).

Tiny homes: April 2026 the province cancelled 200 tiny homes in Miltonvale Park (wetland, the jail next door, neighbours), announced 25 would go to Hillsborough Park without telling anyone (not even the mayor), then cancelled that a week later; the homes had sat 'neglected' for over a year; they went to Slemon Park.

New $180M garbage-burning plant (Enwave) on Riverside Drive, working 2028, 'the envy of the world' (CEO); already 3 years behind and over budget in 2022. The old 42-year-old plant will be kept, decommissioned.
Access PEI's Riverside Drive office closed by water leaks in Oct 2020 and again in May 2026.
Ironwood Estates on Kensington Road billed 'affordable' at $1,385-1,485 a month for a two-bedroom (2021), with a $19.2M federal loan; tenants' group: 'It's not affordable housing at all.'
Stratford: residential property tax up for a third year in a row (2026 budget, last year of a two-cents-a-year plan).
